rows.description: A new wife living with in-laws gives up routines, privacy and sometimes her career to fit in while missing her own family. Adjustment works best when duties are shared fairly and her voice is heard.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult keeps close ties with the extended family through calls, festivals and support while living separately. Closeness is chosen and kept by effort, not by walls or by shared address alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child is taught to say didi, bhaiya, uncle, aunty or ji instead of names for older people. The child copies the sounds first and understands only later that the words carry warmth and rank.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child stays quiet when an elder scolds even when the scolding is unfair, because talking back is seen as disrespect. Fear and respect mix, and the child may swallow feelings that show up later as resentment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, fear, resentment

rows.description: A child hears respect your elders whenever adults disagree and cannot see why. Explaining that respect means courtesy and care, not fear, helps the child keep manners without losing their own voice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager asks why a younger person cannot correct an elder who is wrong. The question is honest, but tone matters; respectful disagreement in private is heard better than public argument.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager finds that respect is used to shut down opinions, as in you will understand when you are older. Feeling unheard, the teen either goes quiet or hides things, which harms trust both ways.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult learns to say I see it differently, with honorifics and calm tone kept, instead of choosing between obeying and rebelling. Politeness carries the message so the elder can hear it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young employee calls seniors sir or madam, holds back objections in meetings and wonders whether silence is respect or fear. Learning when to speak up politely is a skill of the workplace.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: admiration, fear, curiosity, awe

rows.description: A junior watches an elder who listens, admits errors and asks opinions, and gives that person real respect without being told. Respect that is earned lasts; demanded respect breeds hidden mockery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
